summary: Phase 3.7.4 — Orion Operations Center Polish & Reliability verified end-to-end on preview (https://realm-deploy.preview.emergentagent.com). Backend: 11/11 pytest pass (10-check health, 30s cache + ?fresh=1 bypass, founder-only RBAC 200/403/401, CSV export for queries + actions with correct headers and Content-Disposition, user filter, no spurious provider_switch rows). Cold-call health latency measured at ~50ms (well below 500ms budget). Frontend: Admin Hub pill renders 'WARNING' (amber) with title `Orion: Warning · provider=OPENAI · checked 0.1s ago` (correct — llm_provider passes, supabase fails as expected in preview, so amber not red). /admin/orion → Settings shows 10 color-coded health rows (orion-cc-health-{widget_registry,chat_config,llm_provider,sidebar_ids,dashboard_tiles,palette_entries,mongodb,r2_storage,supabase,backend_api}), refresh button issues GET /api/admin/orion/health?fresh=1. Quick Actions search filters tiles ('badge' → only Draft Badge), pin button toggles `orion-tile-pin-on` class, Favorites group renders, localStorage key `orion-cc-quick-favorites=["draft_badge"]` persists across reload (pin-on retained, Favorites group still visible). Tile launch dispatches to Orion Chat (chat view active). CSV export downloads `orion-queries-2026-06-27.csv` from /admin/orion-logs. Cmd+K palette opens. No regressions to Phase 3.7.1-3.7.3.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminOrion.jsx startup validation (line 211-228) logs `[Orion] backend health check failed: [supabase…]` on /admin/orion mount in preview because supabase env vars are intentionally missing — agent context note confirms this is expected. However, the review-request spec item #11 says the expected log line is `[Orion] backend health check ok (10 checks).` — this only fires when EVERY check passes. In preview this never fires; only a console.error with the supabase failure is logged. Functionally correct (graceful fallback, UI not blocked), but the spec wording is misleading. Suggest splitting the log: always log `ok (N checks, M failed=[...])` at info level, and demote the error to a warn so it doesn't pollute Sentry. Minor.

orion_health.py:_run_all_checks (line 191-208) has a slightly awkward optimization: when widget exists, the registry check is computed synchronously (line 201-204), but when missing it's appended to the coroutine list. This is correct but the `async_results[-1]` indexing depends on coroutine append order — currently safe since only mongo+registry are gather'd, but a future check addition could break it. Suggest using a named dict (gather names → results). Minor maintainability.

orion_logs.py CSV export uses `iter([buf.getvalue()])` (line 167) — this materializes the full CSV in memory before streaming. For limit=20000 this could be ~5MB. Fine for current scale but a true streaming writer (chunked DictWriter over the cursor) would be more memory-friendly for larger exports. Non-blocking.

AdminOrion.jsx Quick Actions search input has no clear button visible in the test (data-testid orion-cc-quick-clear-favs exists but not a search-clear). UX nit: typing then deleting works fine, but a (×) inside the search field would be cleaner. Cosmetic.

OrionStatusPill on AdminHub.jsx polls every 30s — that's aligned with the backend cache TTL, so each poll hits cache=true after the first founder visit. Smart. Recommend also surfacing the failing check name in the tooltip when status='Warning' (currently shows only 'provider=OPENAI · checked 0.1s ago' — adding 'failing=supabase' would let the founder know what's amber-warning without clicking through to Settings).
orion_health.py DASHBOARD_TILES IDs now match QUICK_TILES IDs (founder_briefing/investor/draft_badge/draft_widget/announcement/support_digest) — the iter66 inconsistency is RESOLVED. ✅

success_rate.frontend: 100% (pill / 10 health rows / refresh fresh=1 / search / pin / favorites / localStorage persistence / chat dispatch / CSV download / cmd+k all pass)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 3.7.4 confirmed GREEN on preview. Note for future testers: AdminOrion sidebar nav data-testids are `orion-cc-nav-{id}` (NOT `orion-nav-{id}` as the review-request used). Health rows are `orion-cc-health-{check_name}` plus two container elements `orion-cc-health-meta` and `orion-cc-health-grid` (12 total query_selector matches, but only 10 are check rows). localStorage key for favorites is `orion-cc-quick-favorites` (JSON array of tile ids). Supabase failing in preview is expected → pill shows 'Warning' amber, NOT 'Provider Down'. The frontend startup validation's `[Orion] backend health check ok (10 checks).` log will only appear when supabase env vars are wired (i.e. on production); in preview it will instead log a console.error with the supabase failure detail — this is functionally correct.

checks_performed.be_health_10_checks_with_correct_keys: PASS (widget_registry, chat_config, llm_provider, sidebar_ids, dashboard_tiles, palette_entries, mongodb, r2_storage, supabase, backend_api)
checks_performed.fe_admin_orion_settings_10_health_rows_c: PASS (10 rows + refresh button + meta/grid containers)
checks_performed.fe_quick_actions_localStorage_persists_a: PASS (orion-cc-quick-favorites=["draft_badge"], pin-on retained, Favorites group present)
checks_performed.fe_health_log_line_on_mount: EXPECTED-VARIANT — preview logs `console.error [Orion] backend health check failed: [{supabase fail}]` instead of the spec's `ok (10 checks)` line, because supabase env vars are intentionally absent. Functionally correct; will become 'ok (10 checks)' on prod where supabase is wired.

rca of the issue: No bugs. All Phase 3.7.4 features confirmed working on preview. The single 'failed health check' console error is the documented + expected behaviour for preview (supabase env vars missing) — the agent context note explicitly calls this out, and the pill correctly renders amber 'Warning' rather than red 'Provider Down' because llm_provider still passes. Backend cold-call latency is well within the 500ms budget (~50ms over the public preview URL). CSV export Content-Disposition uses backend filename format (orion-queries-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.csv); the browser saved as `orion-queries-2026-06-27.csv` indicating the frontend may also force a date-only filename via the blob save — either way, the spec requirement of `orion-queries-*.csv` is met.
